text: THE Attorney General has returned from Europe. Interviewed as he landed at New York, he seized the opportunity to again decry the ease with which firearms can be obtained in this country, and to reiterate his intention of trying to have Congress pass a national "Sullivan Law." Speaking over a nationwide radio hook-up a few nights later, he used the familiar phrase "To permit the present situation to continue indefinitely amounts to a disclaimer of national intelligence." The Attorney General says that the "great American underworld is armed to the teeth" partly with 2,047 firearms and 273,326 rounds of ammunition stolen from National Guard Armories since January 1, 1933. He infers that this is one outstanding reason for having a Federal Sullivan Law. What he has so far neglected to tell the American people is that the theft of Federal property is already amply covered by Federal law. The Attorney General has also failed to tell the American people that the use of a firearm in connection with resisting arrest by a Federal officer or the robbery or attempted robbery of a National Bank; the conveyance of a firearm into any Federal penal institution; the interstate flight of any person to avoid prosecution for murder, kidnapping, burglary, assault with a dangerous weapon, and other felonies - all are already subject to Federal arrest and prosecution. The Attorney General has also maintained a discreet silence relative to the fact that his assistant, Mr. Joseph B. Keenan, appeared before the Senate Commerce Committee during the last session to oppose Senate 3, a Federal firearms bill which would have made it a Federal offense to transport from one state to another arms with the serial numbers defaced, or stolen firearms and ammunition, whether stolen from Federal or private stocks. Also for any fugitive from justice to transport a firearm interstate or to receive one so shipped; or for any person to steal any firearm while in interstate commerce, or to pawn or receive in pawn any firearm so stolen. By remaining silent on this point the Attorney General saves himself the necessity of explaining to the American people that the reason his assistant opposed Senate Bill No. 3 was not because it was bad legislation - Mr. Keenan admitted that it "would represent a very great advance" - but merely because the bill was not what the Attorney General wanted! Claiming on the one hand to be greatly perturbed by the lack of laws, the Attorney General deliberately opposes a law admitted to be "a very great advance"! Is this sincerity -or merely evidence of the low opinion held by the Attorney General of our "national intelligence" and the intelligence of our elected representatives in the United States Congress who have twice rejected the Attorney General's bill in favor of more sane legislation? Nor will it assist the Attorney General's campaign to urge European practices as a desirable model for America to copy. A Europe whose firearms laws permit the domination of an entire nation by the favored few who are granted the privilege of possessing arms by the party in power, does not appeal to the American people as a model worthy of copying. The splendid Bureau of Investigation of the Department of Justice is now urgently in need of additional men and equipment to enforce the laws already in effect. The sportsmen of America will cheerfully support any appropriations the Attorney General may request to increase the size and training of the Bureau of Identification. Similarly they will continue to support Senator Copeland's Senate Bill No. 3 which will close the iron ring of Federal jurisdiction around the armed crook. But in his insistence upon a particular type of Federal Firearms Law that he wants (the "Sullivan Law" on a national scale) the Attorney General will continue to face the united opposition of sportsmen and of many of the outstanding police and judicial officers in America.
explanation: The text discusses the Attorney General's push for a national 'Sullivan Law' to regulate firearms, critiques existing laws, and opposes new federal firearms legislation, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: "The liberties of our country, the freedom of our civil constitution are worth defending.... We have received them as a fair inheritance from our worthy ancestors: they purchased them for us with toil and danger and expense of treasure and blood.... It will bring an everlasting mark of infamy ...if we should suffer them to be wrested from us by violence without a struggle, or be cheated out of them by the artifices of false and designing men." - Samuel Adams, 1771 Freedom is never free. Since America's Revolution, our hard-won liberty has always come at a great cost. As citizens, we proudly pay the price for freedom when our nation calls, and as members of the National Rifle Association we have paid to protect our liberty from being eroded from within. That's why the NRA is such a peerless force in protecting the Bill of Rights. An English friend - who helplessly watched his firearm freedom evaporate - recently told me that the difference between England's loss of liberty and our success in protecting the individual right to keep and bear arms is defined in a single name: the National Rifle Association of America. If the NRA were ever to shut down or if we ever cut back the vital work we do to preserve freedom, he warned, America could well go the way of Great Britain. In the NRA, we have a force and a power to control our destiny that never existed in England, nor in Australia, where firearm owners are now being forced to submit to new confiscation of registered guns by a government bent on total civil disarmament. NRA's strength is defined by you-by your willingness to vote; to participate in the democratic process; to make your voices heard; to influence your families, friends and co-workers; to reach out to the media with the truth. And there is something else just as important. Money. NRA cannot win without it or survive without it. And the Second Amendment will die without it. Since our stunning election victories in 2000, when we defeated the anti-gun Clinton dynasty, and in 2002, when we strengthened pro-gun majorities in the U.S. House and Senate, the media has painted our current era as a "peacetime" for gun owners. Indeed, NRA has fought hard to pass legislation to end malicious lawsuits designed to destroy the nation's law-abiding firearm industry. We have worked to undo the bureaucratic harm inflicted under the iron fist of the Clinton administration - especially against rural communities and rural citizens when it forced thousands of small, law-abiding, federally licensed gun dealers out of business. NRA spoke out to stop the Federal Communications Commission from allowing international media conglomerates to absorb thousands of independent broadcasters and print news outlets, creating monopoly ownership that could muzzle our defense of our Second Amendment freedoms. And we are at the door of the U.S. Supreme Court to restore our voice silenced by the so-called Campaign Finance Reform Act. With all of this, the media has ginned up the notion that there are no immediate threats to our freedom. Consider the media spin on impending automatic sunset a year from now of the 1994 Federal gun ban on semi-automatic firearms. We all read stories that victory is "in the bag." Nothing is ever "in the bag" - the gun prohibitionists are working tirelessly to keep and expand their ban to include provisions that would turn America into England and Australia overnight. The enemies of the Second Amendment are never "at peace," and the NRA can never be a "peacetime" army. We can never afford to neglect our strength, for a weakened NRA is the fondest dream of America's gun prohibitionists. Today, many firearm owners are living under a false sense of security, lulled by the media into thinking that unless the threat is immediate, there is no need to contribute funds to support the guardians of our rights. Yet, the victories we have delivered have been costly, cutting deeply into NRA's budgets. Winning takes millions of dollars beyond what individual members' dues cover. Today, if we were faced with a full-blown legislative assault, we simply would not have the war-chest to meet the crisis. When we ask for donations-either to NRA or to the NRA Institute for Legislative Action - it is out of absolute necessity. Some NRA members tell me they are tired of fund-raising appeals. And what I tell them - one on one - is the simple truth: Without your donations - without the financial support of individual NRA members, without dollars from supporters of the Second Amendment - NRA would cease to exist. If that day ever comes, the likes of the Brady Campaign, the Violence Policy Center, Americans for Gun Safety and the billionaires and foundations who bankroll them would be dancing on the Second Amendment's grave. Freedom is never free. It always comes at a great cost. Freedom fully depends on your financial and active support. It's just that simple.
explanation: The text focuses on the NRA's role in protecting the Second Amendment, fundraising, and political influence, but does not specifically address gun regulation laws or proposals.

text: Marksmanship training for all American citizens who would be subject to service in the event of war is a valuable contribution to national defense. To prepare ourselves for the variety of military engagements in which we might become involved, we are obliged to maintain a corresponding variety of capabilities within our defense establishment. We must have a stable and continuing defense program because we cannot rely on 'crash programs' in the future. We require the capability to meet any challenge promptly, vigorously, and effectively. National defense is an immediate requirement. What we do today vitally affects our success in any future emergency. In any type of military operations, one thing that has not changed is the importance of the soldier's mastery of his individual weapons, fundamentally the rifle. In fact, this importance has increased. One of the basic requirements of modern warfare is the greatly increased dispersion of units. In order to minimize the effectiveness of an enemy's firepower, our units will be dispersed over a much larger area than ever before. As a result, they will have to be more completely self-sustained and their members will be called upon to exercise an even higher degree of individual self-reliance. Cannoneers, cooks, and clerks must be ready and able to defend themselves against sudden enemy raids. As for the infantryman himself, the rifle is still his basic weapon. We must not forget that the military purpose of war is to achieve control over land and the people who live on it. The ultimate measure of the control which has been attained is the area dominated by the infantryman with the fire of his individual weapon. In the final analysis, the success with which that domination is established, maintained, and extended depends in large part on the soldier's mastery of his rifle. The marksmanship programs conducted by the National Board for the Promotion of Rifle Practice and the National Rifle Association of America for military personnel and civilians are important to our national defense. Qualification firing is excellent training for military and civilians alike. Formal competition plays an important part in encouraging the development of marksmanship. The Small Arms Firing Schools and the National Rifle and Pistol Matches conducted each year at Camp Perry help to maintain the American tradition of a prepared citizenry, trained to do a soldier's job with a soldier's skill when necessity calls. Because of my responsibilities in the Department of Defense and because of my personal lifetime interest in fine marksmanship, I commend those individuals and organizations that promote marksmanship training in time of peace as a vital contribution to preparedness in case of war. I urge continued efforts by our leaders in the Armed Forces and in civilian life to develop better training methods, to improve equipment, and to encourage greater participation in this important activity.
explanation: The text discusses the importance of marksmanship training for national defense and the role of the NRA in promoting it, but does not address gun regulation.

text: The killing, in Chicago, of 8 nurses by Richard Speck with a knife and by strangulation and the killing, in Austin, of of the 15 persons and wounding of 21 other by Charles Whitman with a knife and a gun are tragedies of modern society. Both killers were obviously deranged mentally, but man's knowledge of the human mind is so limited that ever those with professional training in psychiatry can only surmise the causes of their violent actions. Almost any day one may pick up a newspaper and find reports of violent deaths wrought with various instruments, for example, knives, razors, silk stockings, axes, and guns, by individuals who are described as mentally disturbed. Certainly the time is at hand to seek means by which society can identify, treat, and temporarily isolate such individuals. Obviously, elimination of the instrument by which these crimes are committed cannot arrest the ravages of a psychotic murderer. In our society, it is a legal requirement for physicians to report to local authorities those individuals with communicables diseases so that potential potential sources of danger to society can be identified. Likewise, physicians who treat gunshot wounds are required to report the incidents  to the local police so that proper authorities can he alerted to a danger to society. Certainly physicians who learn of such dangers to society, through psychiatric interviews and procedures, should he required to notify the U.S. Public Health Service or the police of the potential source of danger. The psychiatrist to whom Whitman turned earlier this year discloses that during an interview Whitman revealed his intent to climb the tower of the University of Texas to shoot those individuals he found below. In this comment, society had a warning that it did not heed. The consequence was a terrible tragedy. From the many news reports, it is known that at the time of the shootings in Austin, there were possibly physical sources of some of Whitman's troubles. For example, the autopsy has revealed the presence of a tumor on Whitman's brain. Newspaper accounts have also revealed that at the time of death, Whitman had had in his possession a supply of the amphetamine dexedrine, sometimes referred to as "goof balls". The easy availability of drugs of these types also must be seriously examined. From the reports about the man himself, Whitman is described as an exemplary man - a former altar boy in his church, a Boy Scout leader, an above-average student, a good son and husband. No provision of the Dodd Bill (S. 1592) would have prevented the young man Whitman from obtaining firearms by legal means. It is recognized that no law could be formulated that would prevent a Whitman from obtaining firearms without prohibiting firearms to all persons. Certainly it is contradictory that those who favor passage of the Dodd Bill must first explain that the S. 1592 would not have prevented the tragic shooting in Austin and then urge its passage as a means to control firearms. Governor John Connally of Texas had a noteworthy comment: "This man is dead, and my feelings have nothing to do with this particular instance, but we've reached the point where we tend to coddle our criminals. It's getting to the point where a policeman no longer can feel free to pursue his duties without fear of attack. "We need substantial tightening of our laws dealing with criminals, as far as they concern treatment of crimes in this country." Governor Connally said he was in favor of constitutional rights for accused persons "but these 15 people who died had some constitutional rights, too. They had the right not to be killed by some maniac." The early identification, cure, and treatment of 2 and a half million mentally ill in the United States assumes a new importance of tremendous dimensions. The National Rifle Association urges the Congress to fully study the question and to analyze what appropriate steps can be taken to solve the problem.
explanation: The text critiques the Dodd Bill (S. 1592) and discusses the ineffectiveness of gun control laws in preventing crimes like the Whitman shootings, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: THOSE who have done their best by insinuation to brand the National Rifle Association as a powerful, wicked, unscrupulous "gun lobby," attempted to "laugh out of court" our repeated statement that the criminal element in this country is favorable to the passage of extreme types of anti-gun laws. But - to use an oft-quoted phrase - "Let's look at the record": 1.	The first extreme firearms law passed in this country was the notorious Sullivan Law in New York State. The activities of "Big Tim" Sullivan as a political boss of the old school are commonly known. Sullivan was anything but a reformer. The only thing he ever undertook to reform was the right of honest, reputable citizens and voters to possess guns! 2.	In our editorial of November, 1934, we discussed the background of the notorious Alco Law, proposed in California, which was based entirely upon the opinions expressed by criminals, and was actively publicized and promoted by an organization the publicity for which was being handled by a paroled convict. 3.	Before the mid-western State legislatures convened in their current sessions, there was distributed in that area a draft for another very stringent anti-firearms law. This proposal was put forward by one Elliott Wisbrod. Wisbrod at one time sold firearms of various descriptions, including Thompson sub-machine guns, information in our files indicating that the guns used in the famous St. Valentine Day massacre in Chicago had been originally sold by this man. He has never shown a desire to reform anything except the right of the reputable citizen to possess a gun! 4.	In Illinois another stringent firearms bill has been proposed by State Senator William J. Connors. The Chicago Daily News under date of October 27th, 1934, carried a three-column headline: "Gun Play Adorns Past of Cabinet Through Which King Connors Rules." Under date of February 22d, 1935, The Daily News, in an editorial entitled "Arms and The Senator," says in part: "Territorially, Senator Connors should be able to qualify as an expert on the question of ownership of firearms. Police records indicate that not a few firearms must have been owned by his constituents, or at any rate must have been used on them." 5.	The persistent effort a few years ago of State Senator Samuel Salus to secure the passage of a Sullivan Law to disarm the honest citizens of Pennsylvania, will be recalled. Under date of February 2d, the Philadelphia Inquirer carried a two-column headline: "Salus Tops 8 Cited in Bar's Crime Report," the news item stating that "State Senator Samuel W. Salus and seven other prominent Philadelphia criminal attorneys were yesterday ordered by the Board of Judges of Common Pleas Courts to defend themselves against charges of improper practices in criminal cases." Universal Service, under date of October 6th, carried a story in newspapers throughout the country concerning Communist activities in Russia and the United States, which said in part: "At a meeting at Trotsky Headquarters last week, one speaker boasted 'When we have weakened the country by suppressing its rifle bearers * * * we shall be in a position to go ahead with our plan for setting up a government based on the theories of Karl Marx, Lenin and Stalin." No campaign has been undertaken by the National Rifle Association to gather the above facts by hiring detectives or character-anarchists to pry into the lives of individuals proposing strict anti-fire arms bills. The above are chance observations from past and current history, gleaned from scattered newspaper reports. Can such a collection of incidents be reviewed without raising a question in any sane man's mind as to how deep-rooted and far-flung may be the sinister influence behind the continuing agitation for that type of firearms regulation which would place the honest citizen at the mercy of the armed criminal, the crooked politician, and the petty bureaucrat? We are convinced that the majority of anti-gun laws are proposed by honest, well-meaning persons, but the continued cropping-up of the sinister influence leads to the belief that these well-meaning persons have been hoodwinked more often than they realize, and are supported more often than they would like to believe by those forces within and without the United States which are concerned not at all with the welfare of the American home and American institutions, but rather are bent upon the pilfering and destruction of both.
explanation: The text explicitly discusses the origins of anti-gun laws, their proponents, and the NRA's opposition to such legislation, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: Any loyal American can be justly proud to be associated with the National Rifle Association of America which, since 1871, has established such an outstanding record of public service. Although old in years, it has maintained the strength and vigor of youth. With more than a quarter of a million members, its programs of firearms safety education, marksmanship training, and recreation are reaching more people today than at any time in its history. Its official journal, The American Rifleman, stands as the foremost authoritative publication devoted to the fundamental interests of its members - guns and shooting. Today, the National Rifle Association stands upon the threshold of its greatest opportunities. I am honored to be selected as its Executive Director and pledge the full use of my talents in furthering its objects and purposes. A review of the past 85 years will show a record of distinguished and unique contributions to the national life of America: The NRA has consistently opposed misinformation and ignorance involving anti-firearm legislation. It cooperates with legislative bodies in the drafting of legislation which will be most effective in discouraging the use of firearms by the criminal clement without discouraging the ownership and use of small arms on the part of reputable citizens. The NRA has developed a marksmanship program for youth which brings out those qualities of sportsmanship, fair play, manliness, self-control, and cooperation so essential to success in life. The NRA gathers from cooperative state officials uniform information on the causes of hunting accidents with firearms and promotes the NRA Hunter Safety Course to teach proper gun handling to inexperienced hunters The NRA originated the small arms training program which is currently used by the Armed Forces of the United States and was responsible for the establishment of the National Matches which have been one of the great continuing forces in the development of improved rifles, ammunition, training methods, and marksmanship. The NRA was the force which brought about the establishment of the National Board for the Promotion of Rifle Practice to encourage marksmanship among citizens of the country not ordinarily reached in the military training program. The NRA has created an awareness of the need for small arms practice among law-enforcement agencies and has encouraged mutual respect between law-enforcement officers and law-abiding citizens. The NRA is the governing body of competitive rifle and pistol shooting in this country, promulgating the rules and regulations and recognizing national champions and records. It sponsors the rifle and pistol shooting squads which represent the United States in International competitions. The NRA has broadened its program to include those persons interested in collecting firearms, old and new. No aspect of our national life involving the ownership and use of firearms is untouched by activities of the National Rifle Association. No other organization in its field conducts such a comprehensive program of activities with resulting benefits to its members and to our nation. In communities all over our country individuals and groups are participating in NRA programs under the supervision of qualified leaders who serve without compensation. Unpaid members of the elected Board of Directors and appointed Committees establish the programs and policies which are carried out by a trained and experienced Headquarters Staff. Future opportunities for the Association to render public service will be found in the continued growth of its activities and the continued expansion of its influence. This can be done only by gaining the active support and participation of more people. Every reputable individual who is interested in guns and shooting should be a member of NRA. By working together for a stronger, more influential organization with an ever-increasing membership, we can move forward with confidence in realizing our opportunities.
explanation: The text outlines the NRA's history, programs, and contributions to national life, but does not focus on gun regulation.

text: General George Marshall, Chief of Staff of the United States Army, believes firmly in the value of small arms marksmanship as a part of the basic training of every soldier. Training schedules for all branches provide more time for individual marksmanship instruction than in any previous war. Truck drivers, airplane mechanics, cooks-all are being taught to shoot. Every rifle and every round of ammunition that can be spared from combat requirements is being made available for small arms training. But, in spite of all this, the average soldier and the average officer commissioned from civilian life is not being adequately taught the basic principles of small arms firing. The cause and the cure are both apparent. The cause is a serious lack of properly trained small arms instructors. There exists the desire to teach, but the "know how" is lacking. The well-trained Regular, National Guard and Reserve Officers are scattered over the world. Many have moved into the echelons of higher command. The company officers and non-coms who are responsible for the training of our new levies are young men who have attempted to cram a maze of military knowledge into their non-military heads in a short space of time. The training policy of the Army, practical in peacetime, has been that company officers should supervise all the training of the men in their units. The theory is that such a system creates the proper "team spirit" and develops the confidence of the men in their leaders. But under wartime conditions this theory breaks down. Men are born with different aptitudes. This is an age of specialized skills. It is archaic and unrealistic to say that an American company commander will command the greatest respect of his men by being a jack-of-all-trades though he be master of none. The officer's weapon is command. He must know the capabilities and the limitations of the men, machines and guns which he commands. He must have the imagination, the initiative, the intelligence and the courage to use these tools to destroy the enemy. He must see that his men are fed but he does not need to know how to cook. His men will respect him because he proves himself as a commander, not because he performs some mechanical detail that should be done by a soldier. The cure for our declining standards of small arms instruction is the establishment of permanent instruction cadres on every small arms range at officer and enlisted training centers. These cadres should be composed of officers and men who by reason of age or mild physical infirmities are not suited to combat missions. A small arms firing school should be established in each Service Command to give refresher courses to this small arms instruction personnel so as to insure uniform, efficient instruction throughout the Army. Will the prestige of company commanders suffer? Will the morale of the troops be lower because they have really been taught to shoot by men who know how to teach? Ask the Marines on Guadalcanal. The Marine Corps adopted the "company commanders should instruct their men" theory during the piping times of peace. Came the war, new officers by the hundred, new recruits by the thousand. Small Arms qualifications declined seriously. The Marines reverted to their former system, using over-age men as permanent range instruction cadres. Qualifications immediately climbed to an amazingly high figure. In the Army both the Ordnance Department and the Signal Corps are using the permanent cadre system with excellent results. If we are to avoid a repetition of the disgraceful spectacle of 1918 when Americans went into battle not knowing how to load their rifles or set their sights, something must be done now to establish proper small arms firing schools with permanent training cadres at all Army training centers.
explanation: The text discusses the importance of small arms marksmanship training for soldiers and the need for specialized instructors, but does not address gun regulation.

text: After U.S. Grant became President of the United States in 1869, a number of arms manufacturers presented him with handsome presentation pieces. Among these was the .32 rimfire Smith & Wesson revolver shown on the cover of this issue, and now on display in the NRA Museum in Washington, D.C., through the courtesy of President Grant's great-great-grandson, John G. Griffiths, of Arlington, Va., a shooter, collector and an NRA Life Member. Unlike some other mementos which supposedly belonged to Presidents, there is no question about the authenticity of the gold-inlaid, exquisitely engraved revolver with its pearly grips. Two documents attest to it. One is the original page from Smith & Wesson ledgers, (see cover), confirming that a Model "P/2 pistol, gold, pearl, etc.," went to President Grant Aug. 1, 1870. The other is a letter to Griffiths from Maj. Gen. U.S. Grant, 3rd, USA (Ret'd), grandson of the President and grandfather of Griffiths. In direct, kindly fashion, U.S. Grant 3rd, who died last year, wrote on Apr. 7, 1964: "My dear John - I am glad to be able to certify for you that the .32 cal. gold-inlaid rimfire revolver you have was your great-great-grandfather Grant's and has been passed on to me through my Father, in whose possession it was a cherished souvenir when he died in 1912. It can be identified by its serial number 41993. "I have no inside information as to any anecdotes connected with it, but feel sure he never killed any person or animal with it. . . . In any case. I am glad you have it. as I am sure you will prize it and take good care of it. . . . "Affectionately your Grandfather. - Ulysses S. Grant, 3rd." The Grant S&W came complete with a velvet-lined contoured case made to accommodate the 5-shot revolver and 36 rounds of ammunition. The ammunition is contained in a separate compartment covered by a lid. From the look of it, it might well date from Grant's Presidency. At some subsequent time, someone interested in preserving the firearm as a harmless relic drilled a hole in the side of each of the 3 dozen cartridges and poured out the powder, then returned them to the compartment. General Grant, famed for commanding the Union Armies in the War Between the States, served as President of the United States for 2 terms, 1869-1877. He was President of the National Rifle Association in 1883-1884, thus being the 18th President of the U.S. and the 8th President of the NRA.
explanation: The text describes a historical firearm owned by President Ulysses S. Grant, but does not address gun regulation.

text: During the month of November each year, leaders of the safety movement in America meet in the City of Chicago at the National Safety Congress. These men and women are helping to establish safety as a concrete reality through programmed engineering, education, and enforcement for accident prevention. They are making our nation a safer place in which to live because they are engaged in the fight for life. Accidents rank fourth among the nation's killers. They kill more children aged one to 14 than the 5 major diseases combined; they kill more youths aged 15 to 24 than the total of all other causes of death in that age bracket. Accidents claim one life every 5 minutes. Most lives are lost in traffic; with home, public places, and work following in that order. In 1962, the death rate per 100,000 population for the principal types of accidents were: motor vehicles (22.0); falls (10.7); fires and burns (4.0); drowning (3.4); railroads (1.2); firearms and explosions (1.1); poison gases (0.8); and other poisons (0.9). Because of organized safety efforts, the rate of accidental deaths has dropped over the years in spite of the growth in population. This is true especially in industry where prevention methods have been applied with the greatest precision. On-the-job deaths due to accidents have declined nearly 30% during the past 50 years despite the fact that the work force almost doubled. Likewise, deaths due to firearms accidents have declined 50% during the past 30 years although the number of licensed hunters has more than doubled during the period to over 13 million. A significant factor in the drastic drop in deaths due to firearms accidents is the nationwide NRA Hunter Safety Course which was inaugurated in 1950. Based on the conviction that the educational approach is the most effective method of reducing the number of gun accidents in the hunting field, this program is conducted by the National Rifle Association of America in cooperation with the game departments of 34 states and 2 Canadian provinces. Over 44,000 dedicated NRA Certified Hunter Safety Instructors have taught marksmanship and safe gun handling to more than 2 million individuals who have completed the course. As a result, the death rate due to firearms accidents dropped 21% from 1952 to 1962. Available statistics show that approximately 2000 individuals lose their lives each year due to accidents with firearms. More than half of these accidents, about 55%, occur in the home. For this reason, the NRA Home Firearms Safety Course has been inaugurated. Its purpose is to bring information to those unskilled in the use and handling of firearms in order that they may attain the knowledge necessary to prevent unsafe conditions related to guns in the home. Once again, instruction in firearms safety at the local level will be handled by qualified members of the National Rifle Association of America. Safety is positive. It is doing things the right way. The development of a sense of individual responsibility and an attitude of mind conducive to the avoidance of accidents, and the general promotion of education to increase the safety of men, women, and children is a true public service. It is American in concept and its strength lies in the voluntary participation and active support of all who are in a position to promote safety. Those NRA Certified Instructors who are conducting hunter safety and home firearms safety courses deserve the gratitude and support of all who enjoy guns and shooting. Let us join them in the fight for life.
explanation: The text discusses firearm safety education, the NRA Hunter Safety Course, and its impact on reducing accidents, but does not address gun regulation.

text: Any day now, gun rights leaders in the U.S. Senate will engage in a battle to determine whether the American firearm industry - our source, as consumers, for firearms and related products - will remain viable or will be bankrupted through endless predatory lawsuits that the enemies of Freedom predict will be a "death of a thousand cuts." The watchword in this Senate battle must be "clean." The Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act - S. 397 - must be passed with no "gun control" amendments. No so-called "assault weapons" ban - no breathing new life into the fraudulent Clinton gun ban. No gun show restrictions - no criminalizing of now-legal private sales between law-abiding Americans. No ban on rifles. No ban on small caliber pistols. No back-door gun registration by keeping National Instant Check System (NICS) records indefinitely. Each of us must contact our senators and demand that S. 397 be passed with no "gun control" amendments solely designed to snuff out this long-needed legislative reform. And we must tell our fellow gun owners what this is really about-the future of all lawful commerce in firearms and the future of our ability to exercise our Second Amendment rights. Introduced by U.S. Sens. Larry Craig (R-Idaho) and Max Baucus (D-Mont.), the legislation is co-sponsored by a majority of the Senate. It is the same bill that overwhelmingly passed the U.S. House of Representatives in 2003 by a 285-to-140 roll call vote. And it is the same bill that was withdrawn in 2004 by Second Amendment leaders in the Senate following a series of "poison pill" amendments attached by gun-ban senators - some of whom, like then-Minority Leader and gun-rights chameleon Tom Daschle, didn't survive re-election because of this anti-gun duplicity. The gun-ban crowd is already planning to repeat last year's strategy by adding new killer amendments - many wrapped in the media lie of the day - "terrorism." We will see amendments to close down gun shows and to bring back the Clinton gun ban that we worked so hard to see sunset into oblivion. But their biggest effort will be a ban on now-demonized rifles. When the national media talks about banning what it calls ".50 caliber sniper rifles," they tout California, where mostly single-shot or bolt-action rifles were classified as prohibited "semi-automatic assault weapons." Forget the caliber. This is a rifle ban, and it spells the future. Like any other "gun control," this is incremental - one step at a time. The Violence Policy Center is already calling for a ban on what it calls "intermediate sniper rifles"... which it defines as ".30 calibers" (see p. 14). According to the VPC, if you own a bolt-action or semi-auto hunting rifle, you own an "intermediate sniper rifle." And the first step in this rifle ban - on the federal level - will be offered as an amendment to S. 397. Senators Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y), Hillary Clinton (D-N.Y.), Frank Lautenburg (D-N.J.) and John Kerry (D-Mass.) will be screaming about "terrorism," but the real terror to be inflicted on America is their assault on our liberty. When the enemies of Freedom try to defend their reckless lawsuits, they talk about victims. But when it comes to victims of genuine negligence or defective products, there is nothing in S. 397 to keep anyone from going to court and filing a legitimate claim. What will end are abusive claims against innocent third parties who violate no law and who have no connection with street criminals and violence. In all these suits, honest business people are supposed to pay a punitive price simply for being in the highly regulated federal firearm business. The Washington Post summed this up with a concise description of a case involving the mother of a boy injured with a gun that was never found - a pistol that was the centerpiece of a years - long lawsuit against every element of the firearm industry, which cost tens of millions of dollars to successfully defend. "She does not blame ... the adult who bought it illegally or the gun trafficker who sold it out of a car trunk. Instead her rage is aimed at the firearms industry ... ." That suit - a model for dozens filed in activist courts by big-city mayors and greedy trial lawyers - was heavily funded by globalist gun banner George Soros and supported by the Brady Campaign. "Rage aimed at the firearm industry" has cost consumers well over $200 million, and it will ultimately financially bleed out the industry ... if Congress doesn't move decisively. As NRA members, we are in the vanguard of tens of millions of firearm owners-consumers all who are directly harmed by these extortionary lawsuits. Remember the words of John Coale, Washington fat-cat trial lawyer: "The legal fees alone are enough to bankrupt the industry." As we enlist the help of our family, coworkers and friends in contacting their senators, we must make it clear that this legislation - which protects all our rights - must pass the U.S. Senate with no anti-gun amendments. Call, write, e-mail today.
explanation: The text discusses the Protection of Lawful Commerce in Arms Act (S. 397) and opposes amendments that would impose gun control measures, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: PUBLIC OPINION is the most powerful influence in the world. Did you ever ask yourself "What makes 'public opinion'?" Newspapers? Then how could Franklin D. Roosevelt have been four times elected President of the United States with the majority of newspapers opposing him? Radio? Then why does radio so often find it advisable to change its programs or to 'put the brakes on' some noted commentator? Political speeches? How many times has a political speech caused you to change your opinion? The truth is that public opinion is the product of what the people, individually and in family groups, see, feel, and discuss among themselves. It is "grass roots" stuff! In every family there is one person, be it parent, child, or boarder, whose opinions are given particular weight on particular subjects. In every luncheon club, in every card club, in every shop and in every board of directors, the opinions of certain individuals are particularly respected on certain subjects. In the day-to-day contacts of these and similar groups of everyday citizens at home, at work, and at play, public opinion is unconsciously but inevitably formed. Public opinion is the only force that can put an end to the recurrent efforts of the oddly assorted group who take advantage of every opportunity to foist a Gestapo-type of firearms registration on the American citizen. You, Mr. and Mrs. Shooter, can mold that public opinion and you must mold it because you are in the family group, the club, the shop, the board of directors where public opinion is made. In each such group you are probably the person who best understands and can most intelligently discuss the many angles involved in a question so seemingly simple as gun registration. Is the 'public opinion' of your group strong about guns and their use? Then you must straighten out their thinking because only you are in a position to do so! All year 'round we receive forceful letters, splendidly logical letters, from sportsmen complaining about proposed legislation, newspaper editorials, or statements by local officials concerning antifirearms proposals. These letters tell us why the writer is opposed to antigun laws. We have published through the years most of those arguments. So why take the time to write us? Why not write the same letter but address it to the legislator, the newspaper editor, the local official who needs to know that 'public opinion' is not all on his side? Whether or not he knows it, the average member of the NRA and reader of The Rifleman is a man better informed on guns and gun laws than most of his acquaintances. Hundreds of NRA stalwarts have told us that they revel in their positions as gun oracles for the community. Since this is true, you hold in your hands, individually, the power to mold public opinion in a direction that will eliminate for a long time the spectre of antigun legislation. Have you ever discussed the matter at the family dinner table? Have you encouraged the youngsters to discuss it in debates or theme papers at school? What do your fellow members in the Chamber of Commerce know about it? Or in the Bar Association? Or in the men's club at church? Or the men and women with whom you discuss politics, vacations, and wages at the shop or office? Public opinion is being formed all about you all the time! You, not the editor of The American Rifleman, reach the people who aren't shooters but who are 'public opinion.' Keep a tally, and you will be very happy at the end of just one month to count how many have said to you, "By golly, you are right! I never realized there was so much to this gun registration business. From now on I'm against it!" Public opinion is the most powerful force in America. There is no magic about it. It grows up from the grass roots!
explanation: The text explicitly discusses public opinion on gun registration and the NRA's role in opposing it, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: A few unscrupulous gun merchants are creating a serious situation for law-abiding citizens who believe in the right to keep and bear arms. 'Mail-order guns' have become a national issue. Shocking reports are being published in newspapers and magazines exposing the tactics of a small number of mail-order houses involved in interstate shipment of cheap handguns to juveniles, criminals, and mental defectives. These junk guns are being imported into America and offered for sale mostly through advertisements in comic books and pulp magazines. Orders are handled by mail, often addressed to a post-office box. Shipments usually are made by common carrier since Federal postal regulations prohibit the shipment of firearms by mail except to certain specified military and enforcement officers or to bona fide dealers and manufacturers. Most of the information being publicized relative to these gun merchants and their customers has been made available by studies and hearings conducted during the past several years by the Senate Subcommittee to Investigate Juvenile Delinquency. Much of the testimony of witnesses and reporting by writers borders on sensationalism, with the usual emotional reactions. Nevertheless, there is concrete evidence that a serious problem does exist and responsible leaders intend to do something about it. The latest proposal, aimed at irresponsible purchasers, is to amend the Federal Firearms Act to make it unlawful for any manufacturer or dealer to ship a handgun in interstate or foreign commerce to anyone without a Federal firearms license unless that person has submitted a sworn statement, attested by a notary public, to the effect (1)	that such person is 18 years or more of age; (2) that he is not a person prohibited from receiving a firearm in interstate or foreign commerce; and (3) that there are no provisions of law, regulations, or ordinances applicable to the locality of the purchaser which would be violated by such person's receipt or possession of the handgun. It also would be unlawful for any person to cause to be transmitted by mail or in interstate or foreign commerce such a sworn statement which contains any false statement as to any material fact for the purpose of obtaining a handgun. Another proposal, aimed at the unprincipled gun merchant, is to increase the fee for obtaining a Federal firearms license to $50 for a manufacturer or pawnbroker and to $10 for a dealer. Manufacturers and dealers would be required to give written notice to the common or contract carrier when a handgun, is being shipped in interstate or foreign commerce. It would be unlawful for the carrier to deliver such a handgun to any person with knowledge or with reasonable cause to believe that such person is under 18 years of age. Steps must be taken to stop the traffic of mailorder guns into unauthorized hands. At the same time, due caution must be exercised so that law-abiding citizens are not severely penalized or deprived of their individual rights. Reputable gun owners long have contended that accidents and crimes with firearms cannot be prevented by passing laws aimed at the gun. It is reassuring that proposed solutions to this particular situation are being directed at irresponsible merchants and purchasers. With this approach, steps can be taken toward a reasonable solution to the problem of mail-order guns.
explanation: The text discusses proposed amendments to the Federal Firearms Act to regulate mail-order guns, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: It is mostly thoughtlessness, it is partly a deliberate effort to create dissension, but whatever the cause there are many Americans who seem to be currently more interested in the fact that they are political officeholders, or bankers, or 'workers' (who isn't?), or merchants, or farmers, than they are interested in the fact that they are first and foremost Americans. February is a good month to remember what it means to be an American. Within the short span of ten days we celebrate, this month, the birthdays of the two men who, more than any others, symbolize for Americans the things which are America. The birthday of Washington, landed aristocrat who risked personal fortune, reputation, life itself, to lead a quarreling, badly organized lot of backwoodsmen, farmers, middle-class merchants, and country gentlemen to moral victory over their own disunity, to military victory over the world's greatest military power, and to the formation of that republic which relighted the beacon of freedom for men all over the world. The birthday of Lincoln, impoverished son of the frontier, who availed himself of the opportunities afforded by that republic to even its lowliest sons and rose to the highest elective office in the gift of his fellow citizens - leading them then through that bloody struggle which preserved the Union and the freedom of the individual that Washington had risked so much to establish. It is fortunate coincidence that, so early in each year, Americans are reminded of the lives of these two men - so superficially different, so fundamentally alike. One to the manor born; the other an orphaned wanderer from cabin to cottage. One carefully garbed in the height of fashion; the other careless of garb in work-a-day clothes. One meticulous in his books of account, canny in his bargaining; the other most interested in the books of the sages, prone to bargain poorly. Each, in his own way, prideful of accomplishment, fine in resolve, a purposeful gambler. Together typifying the whole broad range of qualities, of opportunities, of accomplishments which have made America great. This year, may February 12 and February 22 mean more to us than just some more holidays. May they be days for a hit of personal soul-searching. As we celebrate these birthdays may we quietly, without smugness, without bigotry, resolve to take renewed pride in the simple fact that we are Americans - sole heirs to the traditions, the opportunities, the responsibilities symbolized by George Washington, landed gentleman, and Abraham Lincoln, orphan of the frontier.
explanation: The text reflects on the meaning of being an American and the legacies of George Washington and Abraham Lincoln, but does not address gun regulation.

text: The impressive citizens' commission that President Lyndon B. Johnson has appointed to search out the causes of violence has our heartfelt support. As an organization of a million sportsmen dedicated to the safe and sane use of firearms for pastime, the National Rifle Association laments every misuse of guns more than most. It also knows that guns play a minor part in the current tidal wave of violence. The commission will find that murder continues to increase in metropolitan areas that have placed severe restrictions on firearms and that, even so, gun killings are only about half what they were 30 or 40 years ago in relation to our population size. Perhaps the most significant point is that while violence has taken a startling upswing, there probably are fewer firearms per capita in the U.S. now than in much of the 2-gun frontier past. Obviously, then, something other than guns, which have been with us all along, must be responsible. To be blunt, we believe that the commission in its search need look no farther than the nearest television screen. TV is not wholly to blame, of course, but its 2 largest networks in particular have worked up a national frenzy. Never before in the long history of mankind has the human mind been subjected to the explosive effect of so much violence, viciousness and depravity before its eyes. Never before have the goriest crimes been projected into the American home in gruesome detail as news, and then warmed over to regale as "entertainment" in fiction form. "In Cold Blood" could be the slogan of much of the television industry. Its effect as a blatant stimulant to law-breaking is suggested in 2 sentences from authoritative sources: 1. Youngsters in the 12-17 age group spend 18 to 20 hours a week watching television, according to the Nielson Television Index. 2.	Approximately the same age group, 11-17, in 1965 committed 61% of all U.S. car thefts, nearly half of the Nation's burglaries and larcenies, 28% of robberies, almost 20% of rapes, and - despite their youth - 8.4% of willful homicides, according to FBI statistics. The older brothers and sisters of this group, aged 18-24, were found by the FBI to have committed more than a quarter of the Nation's homicides and nearly half of its rapes although they form only a tenth of the population. They presumably had spent more years in front of the television. As this magazine pointed out editorially in February, some of the same networks that have smeared legitimate firearms ownership under the guise of protecting the public from guns have televised gunplay, gore and horror galore. This has not escaped notice. The 11-million-member Southern Baptist Convention, in advocating gun controls within constitutional limits, criticized "the glorification and exploitation of violence in television, movies, newspapers and fiction" as "an adverse influence . . . particularly on our youth." U.S. Sen. Ralph Yarborough (Texas), also blaming TV, said, "No generation of Americans has been taught murder like the present generation." The British, whose rigid restraint on gun ownership has been held up by some TV commentators as an example for America, set a more appropriate example that might be applied to American television. British TV is a public utility under a nonpolitical board of directors and with higher standards than in the U.S. While Government operation of television clashes with our private enterprise concepts, the new commission on violence might well recommend that American television either exercise more self-control or be policed by the Federal Communications Commission, which apparently lacks authority to suggest toning down even the wildest programs. Television also can complicate the already-acute problems of guarding public figures even without being over-sensational. Dr. Roger Peel, psychiatrist at Washington's St. Elizabeth's Hospital, where mentally-disturbed persons threatening the White House are sent, blames TV at least in part for a fivefold increase in the number of cases since LBJ took office. Projecting the President's image at people prone to have delusions, Dr. Peel explains, "makes the President more a part of their delusional system" - which is a nice medical way of saying that TV makes menaces out of crackpots. Television has been vivid in keeping fresh the details of the JFK assassination and other murders. So have some other news media. James R. Hendrick, head of the White House Secret Service detail, was quoted: "All of this talk and publicity about assassinations has been bad." That was before Sen. Robert Kennedy's death. Newspapers apparently helped to spark the assassinations of 2 slain Presidents, Lincoln and McKinley, and also the Robert Kennedy death. The suspect in the RFK murder carried with him a news clipping critical of his victim. John Wilkes Booth, who killed President Lincoln, was dejected and infuriated on reading reports of the downfall of the Confederacy. Leon Czolgosz, the crazed anarchist who murdered President McKinley, kept in his pocket and read nightly as his deadly inspiration a newspaper account of how another anarchist had assassinated King Humbert of Italy the previous year. By refraining from sensationalism, the communications media can make an immediate contribution to national security and toward reducing violence. We hope that all, including some that seem to have gone berserk, will manage to do so. The First Amendment is no more a license to arouse criminal passions than the Second Amendment is a permit to misuse firearms.
explanation: The text critiques the media's role in glorifying violence and discusses the causes of violence, but does not focus on gun regulation.

text: It happened Tuesday night, October 5th, as I spoke at the Friends of NRA Banquet in Charlotte, North Carolina. At 7 p.m., while Charlotte-Mecklenburg police officers Anthony Nobles and John Burnette chased a robbery suspect, I told North Carolina the horrible truth: their state is nearly first in violent crime nationwide - and dead last in doing something about it. As the suspect hid in the woods to ambush the officers, I was pledging the full force of NRA to overhaul the state's criminal justice system. As the suspect jumped officer Burnette and went for his gun, I was telling North Carolina that NRA will demand action. Before I finished speaking, Nobles and Burnette were killed. The suspect in the slayings that has filled a state with fury? Alden Jerome Harden. On probation for a 1992 armed robbery - plea-bargained down to robbery. Arrested 19 times in the last 10 years - convicted only nine times. Sentenced to seven years in 1992 - sentence suspended. And when he violated parole last spring, when he could have been sent straight to prison, a Mecklenburg County judge sent him to the streets. This is the face of crime in America: assault, arrest, release. Armed robbery, plea bargain, release. Probation violation, arrest, release. The latest cop killer may be behind bars, but his accomplice - a runaway criminal justice system - is still on the loose. And the new sentencing reform just passed in North Carolina won't do the job. Prison time will still be too short. Many who should go to prison won't. Even for assault with intent to kill, prison is optional. Even if imprisoned for this vicious crime, release is possible after five days in prison. To the people of North Carolina, and especially to the families of officers Burnette and Nobles, I pledge action: Real Juvenile Justice. It's time to scrap a system designed for pranksters who stole hub caps and replace it with one for gangsters who rape and kill. Tougher Sentences. NRA CrimeStrike helped double actual time served for violent offenders in Texas and abolish parole in Arizona. We can do it in North Carolina. "3 Strikes,	You're Out!" CrimeStrike is the muscle behind the Washington state initiative to put three-time losers away for life. We can do it in North Carolina. Above all, NRA and CrimeStrike will make a simple appeal to the governor and the legislature. Years ago, the state settled with the Feds and imposed a prison cap that set criminals free and sent crime skyrocketing. Lift that cap. There is no reason that violent predators have to be housed any better than law-abiding poor people. We will insist that politicians honor their police, their citizens and their state. We will insist: lift that cap. The families of these officers know too well the brutal face of crime. One day soon, they will recognize the face of law and order. Its initials: NRA.
explanation: The text discusses crime, sentencing reform, and the NRA's CrimeStrike program, but does not address gun regulation.

text: The past year has been the most gratifying of my 14 years at NRA. NRA is back! And we're growing as never before. For the first time ever, we've had three consecutive quarters of growth, adding 600,000 new members. And for the first time, we're about to surpass three million paid members. On the legislative front, not one anti-gun bill passed in Congress. NRA programs have been revitalized with new leadership and ideas. Change has made us stronger and more responsive to our members Some of the most important changes in your Association are in our programs. We expanded and improved NRA International Shooting to make our shooters the top contenders at the 1996 Olympic Games. Under new leadership, our Hunter Services Division completed the NRA Whitetail Tour and NRA SuperClinic. These two programs have been combined into the most comprehensive hunting program ever presented, the 1993 NRA Great American Hunter Tour, with events in over 60 cities and nearly 40 states. The Young Hunter Marksmanship Program came on line, and the new Hunter Clinic Instructor Program took top honors as an educational tool to advance hunter safety, ethics and responsibility. And our Youth Hunter Education Challenge reached out to some 15,000 young hunters. The Eddie Eagle Gun Safety Program received fresh new materials and an animated video starring Eddie and teen sensation Jason Priestly. Already distributed to almost four million children, the Eddie Eagle program will not achieve the national prominence it deserves. The high point for competitions was the saving of the National Matches at Camp Perry, Ohio. As the 85th Anniversary Matches came to a close in August, we were assured that this American tradition will continue. Law Enforcement Activities and Relations were combined into a single division. As instructor certification continued, we took the lead with NRA CrimeStrike to defeat Time Warner's irresponsible promotion of a "cop killer." A new NRA division was formed to promote recreational shooting and range development and to enhance our coach and instructor programs. We moved ahead with Sporting	Clays.	And the range assistance program has grown with the advent of the NRA Range Technical Team and the development of new ways to build ranges for all Americans to enjoy the shooting sports. Your Association now has a talented mix of experience and new ideas that has allowed us to take the same leadership position in the shooting sports we've held so long on the legislative front. I appreciate all your encouragement and support. Next year I intend to meet even more of your in person, and I look forward to sharing your ideas for the future of the National Rifle Association. NRA is a cause. Our Cause.
explanation: The text outlines the NRA's achievements, programs, and growth, but does not address gun regulation.

text: We have often pointed out that the oddly assorted group who urge the political registration of privately owned small arms base their propaganda largely on half-truths and innuendo. This, of course, is the outstanding characteristic of the Communist line, as it was of the Fascist and Nazi propaganda. Not for a moment do we imply that all proponents of the OGPU and GESTAPO type of firearms registration are either Communists or Fascists. Many are sincere, well-intentioned do-gooders, simple-minded enough to fall victims to the same kind of fallacious sophistry as turned other well-intentioned citizens into pawns for the Mussolini-Hitler-Lenin triumvirate. Currently the most popular argument in favor of the central bureau registration of privately owned small arms is "returning veterans have brought so many weapons into the country that a terribly dangerous problem has been created." The intimation is that today there are more guns per family in America than ever before. It is true that a lot of guns of varying descriptions were brought home by men from overseas. But, examine the situation in the cold light of fact rather than in the dim shadow of propaganda and a very different picture emerges. Everyone knows, though they seem to have forgotten, that not a single rifle, shotgun, or pistol was manufactured or imported for sale to American sportsmen and farmers during the war years! Under normal conditions of manufacture and importation, several hundred thousand brand-new guns, in excellent operating condition, chambered for readily obtainable American ammunition would have been placed in American families between 1942 and 1945. Would the police have felt that this perfectly normal situation posed any new or terribly dangerous problem in law enforcement? They would never have given it a thought. Why then raise a frantic storm over the veterans' ill-assorted collection of shotguns, rifles, and pistols, mostly chambered for ammunition which is not available in this country and in many cases unserviceable because they were assembled from parts picked up hither and yon on battlefields and abandoned production lines? Consider also the fact that during the war it was almost impossible to get spare parts, or to have dependable repairs made on the guns which were in shooters' hands from prewar days. Too, there were thousands of guns left in the inexperienced hands of wives and mothers to be kept free of rust during the years that husbands and sons were in uniform. The results in many cases have been tragic from the viewpoint of the returning gun-lover. Unquestionably the rate of attrition for small arms owned by reputable Americans was far greater between 1942 and 1945 than during any similar period in peacetime. Finally, it should be remembered that American sportsmen sold and donated several thousand, rifles, shotguns, and pistols to the American and British Governments for the arming of internal security units in the early days of the war. All of these weapons were permanently taken out of the normal stock of privately owned weapons. When all the facts are thus considered, the ''serious situation" so persistently played up by the gun-registration group takes on the old familiar aspect of propaganda by half-truth and innuendo. The arguments of the antigun crowd always lose their force when the record is kept straight.
explanation: The text critiques proposals for firearms registration, discussing their origins and the NRA's opposition, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: There has never been better teamwork between those of us who serve in Washington and you, the individual NRA member - the people we serve. The headline in The Washington Post said it all - "House Defeats Gun Control Bill" - in describing the defeat of the Lautenberg / McCarthy gun registration scheme after a week-long legislative battle in the Congress. In all the years I've been with NRA, I've never been prouder of our teamwork. Many US Representatives told me they had never experienced grassroots legislative action from the folks back home like this. Telephone calls, mail, e-mail and faxes into Capitol Hill offices were running anywhere from 100 to one to 500 to one against the White House gun control package. And for once - some in the media got it right. They weren't referring to the "gun lobby" as some back-room "special interest," they were calling us what we are - a grassroots lobby, the voice of the people. Democracy in action. "The NRA does the best job of any group in lobbying members. They don't have marches, they don't have demonstrations, they don't shoot their guns in the air. It's just good, straight democracy." That was the assessment of anti-gun U.S. Rep. Barney Frank (D-MA). Former Clinton spin-meister George Stephanopoulos said, "There's a lot of talk about extremists here. Let me make one small vote for the NRA. They're good citizens. You know what? They call their Congressman. They write. They vote. They contribute. And they get what they want over time." Anti-gun House Minority Leader Richard A. Gephardt (D-MO) told the media, "We're up against the best lobby in town .... My hat is off to them. I admire them. They sure know how to do it." The debate in the House - led courageously by Democratic Congressman John Dingell of Michigan -  demonstrated once again that gun owners' rights cross all political boundaries. While the White House was twisting arms to force a party-line vote, individual Members of Congress listened to their constituents, and 45 Democrats defected from the Clinton-Gore agenda. Even with the Clinton-Gore spin to reshape the "gun control" issue into "gun safety," the big lie didn't work. It was clear that most Americans saw no connection between "gun control" and two twisted teenagers in Littleton, Colorado, who carried out a year-long plan to celebrate Hitler's birthday by slaughtering a dozen of their classmates and planting enough homemade bombs to kill and maim hundreds more. Bill Clinton even admitted that nothing he proposed in the way of gun control would have stopped the two Columbine terrorists who violated a host of state and Federal gun laws before they violated the law against coldblooded murder. For his part, Al Gore attacked the rights of young Americans. The Gore mantra, intoned at a U.S. Conference of Mayors meeting, was designed to bolster support for an amendment to make gun possession by all 18- to 21-year-olds a criminal offense, but Gore got the facts dead wrong - Gore stated that anyone between the ages of 18 and 20 "can walk into any gun shop, any pawn shop, any gun show, anywhere in America and buy a handgun." Of course, federal law has prohibited the purchase of a handgun from a Federal Firearms License (FFL) holder by anyone under the age of 21 since 1968. This big lie didn't wash - even the media pointed out Gore's gaffe, and his office soon issued a "correction." The dynamic of American politics with respect to the firearms rights issue has changed dramatically because of the House vote. A lot of people in politics understand that Barney Frank is right when he says the NRA represents "just good, straight democracy." But not Bill Clinton. And certainly not Al Gore. After the House vote, Clinton vowed to reporters, "This vote will not stand the light of day. I will keep working until Congress stands up to the gun lobby ..." He claimed that the "soundness of our democracy" was at stake, and that "the heart and soul of America is on the line." Indeed it is, but in the opposite of the way he meant it. Bill Clinton's petulant arrogance threatens the principles on which our nation was founded, and commentator George Will made that clear when he remarked "Congress this week worked exactly the way the Founding Fathers designed it. When the American people want something intensely and protractedly, it happens, when they don't it doesn't... that's the way it's supposed to work." But defeat makes Bill Clinton even more dangerous. Because he can't run for another consecutive term for President, he has no accountability to the people for anything. With nothing to lose, he will strike and strike again to poison our liberty. We can't let our guard down for even a moment. In a two-hour ABC "Good Morning America" television appearance with his wife, Hillary, Bill Clinton promised an ever-widening assault on Second Amendment rights. The media focused on his vigorous endorsement of national firearms owner registration, but he demanded far more. "Pretty soon, you will have technology available which you can put into guns ... which will mean that only people who have the right fingerprints can fire the guns. And that will be a huge thing." In the same breath the President said. "Then, we'll have to do a lot of gun buy-back programs and other things ... ." That's what they did in Australia. Firearms registration, followed by mandatory gun turn-ins in the guise of "buy-backs." Clinton will spend his every remaining day in office seeking vengeance for this defeat. Already, anti-gun politicians are demanding another opportunity to attack our rights. We must keep our successful teamwork going, through summer and fall, into the pivotal election year that follows. Together, we can put the Clinton / Gore antigun machine on the scrapheap of history where it belongs.
explanation: The text discusses the defeat of the Lautenberg/McCarthy gun registration scheme and the NRA's opposition to gun control measures, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: All of us ar familiar with noises in the night. They rouse us for a moment but usually prove empty and soon pass. In their attacks on legitimate private firearms ownership, a series of national commissions appointed under the previous administration are likely to prove, in the long march of history, to be no more than noises in the night of humanity. Their only difference is that several have lasted a little long and have alarmed uninformed people and some news media. The latest of these lame-duck commissions to trot out a report is the National Commission on the Reform of Federal Criminal Laws, created in 1966. While some parts of its report may yet serve a useful purpose, its major recommendations on guns read like palpable anti-gun propaganda. The sad part of this is that they are being parrotted as if they possessed significance. Consider the recommendations and then consider the source. The American public is informed in a printed report, made at a cost of $850,000 or more, that a "majority" of the commission advocate confiscation of all privately owned handguns and registration of all long arms. Strangely enough, the number and names of the commission "majority" are not revealed in the report. Why? Who are they? What have they or the commission staff got to hide? For $850,000-plus, the public should be entitled to know. There is a Federal Freedom of Information law. Must it be invoked against an agency with the resoundingly righteous title of National Commission on the Reform of Federal Criminal Laws? By what is at least a rare coincidence, the "reform commission's" gun recommendations are virtually those of a political organization known as Americans for Democratic Action. The ADA can claim to be the first national group to urge confiscation of private handguns, in 1969. So let us consider the source of the reform commission's recommendation on firearms, which some news media have gleefully hailed as "fresh evidence" of a need for more restrictive Federal action on guns. The commission consisted of 12 members, three representing respectively the U.S. Senate, the House, the Federal courts and the public. The last time a vacancy occurred, it was for a Congressman. Speaker McCormack designated Rep. Abner J. Mikva (2d Dist., III.). Rep. Mikva is the prime mover in legislation to "dry up" and eventually eliminate, by legislated harassment, the private ownership of handguns. Rep. Mikva is, or was, also a member of the national board of ADA, the organization favoring handgun confiscation. He introduced two anti-handgun bills last year and put in another on the first day of this session. On the staff side, the director of the commission is a law professor who is almost a "professional" member of commissions, having served on at least five in recent years. He is Dr. Louis B. Schwartz, of Philadelphia. He is the same Dr. Schwartz who was on the national board of ADA, the organization that favored handgun confiscation as far back as 1969. The commission's staff "firearms consultant" is listed as "Frank Zimring". He is the same Franklin E. Zimring, youthful University of Chicago law professor, who concocted the firearms report of the recently defunct and largely unmourned National Commission on the Causes and Prevention of Violence. Zimring spoke out for gun confiscation in Illinois even before he became the "firearms expert" of the socalled violence commission, which was publicized as an "impartial inquiry". Now, one commission later, his views as embodied in the latest report are being billed by some as "fresh evidence". Several others connected with this latest commission are old hands at working with commissions that attack existing firearms ownership. U.S. District Judge A. Leon Higginbotham of Philadelphia, reputedly an able jurist, was a member of both the "reform" and the "violence" commissions. Hon. Patricia Roberts Harris, a former diplomat, served on the violence commission and as a member of the advisory committee of the reform commission. This latter advisory committee was headed by former Associate Justice Tom C. Clark, father of former Attorney General Ramsey Clark, who vied with former U.S. Senators Dodd and Tydings in demanding more gun laws. So it can hardly be said with accuracy that the commission report represents an entirely fresh view of the U.S. firearms situation. Yet that is exactly what some news media and anti-gun spokesmen seem to be saying. Under the title, "Another Voice for Gun Control", the Los Angeles Times editorialized Jan. 15, 1971, that "another Presidential commission has joined the long list" of those seeking tougher gun control laws. The Los Angeles Times supported its firearms editorial by quoting the National Commission on the Cause and Prevention of Violence-that is to say, in connection with firearms, by quoting Frank or Franklin Zimring all over again. Presumably his, this time, was "Another Voice" as mentioned in the title. The overall result contributed to the journalistic smog beclouding the gun issue. And so the tawdry procession of figures shouting against guns emerges again from the wings of the theater that is Washington, D.C., with a new billing and a new name for their act, and they get rave reviews from some anti-gun media. Some day both performers and media may stop and look at the audience. They may be appalled at how small it really is, and how it sits on its hands. So will anybody else who invests political capital in such show ventures.
explanation: The text critiques the recommendations of the National Commission on the Reform of Federal Criminal Laws, which include confiscation and registration of firearms, directly addressing gun regulation.

text: "[A] representative democracy ceases to exist the moment that the public functionaries are by any means absolved from their responsibility to their constituents; and this happens whenever the constituent can be restrained in any manner from speaking, writing or publishing his opinions upon any public measure, or upon the conduct of those who may advise or execute it." - New York Times v. Sullivan That commentary came in a landmark decision by the United States Supreme Court in 1964 that went back to the birth of the nation to shed light on the intent of the Founders on free speech guaranteed by the First Amendment. Those same issues are central to NRA's challenge to the constitutionality of John McCain's so-called campaign finance reform - the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (BCRA). In arguments before a special three-judge panel in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, NRA's legal team argued, "At the heart of the Court's unanimous ruling (in Sullivan) was its recognition that political speech is the lifeblood of our representative democracy and that debate on public issues should be uninhibited, robust and wide open." NRA's fine legal team, principally led by Charles J. Cooper, Cleta Mitchell, and David Thompson, eloquently expressed NRA's defense of liberty in legal briefs submitted on our behalf and in appearances before the court. Though NRA was first among more than 80 organizations and individuals to challenge this oppressive law-including U.S. Sen. Mitch McConnell (R-KY), the American Civil Liberties Union and the AFL-CIO - our single critical thrust is to strike down BCRA's ban on broadcast political speech decreed 60 days before a primary election and 30 days prior to a general election. During the ban period, the broadcast of political speech the government might declare as "electioneering communication" - speech that refers to an identifiable candidate - would be a crime. Our case, part of a consolidated challenge - McConnell v. FEC - is headed to the United States Supreme Court under a congressionally mandated accelerated schedule.
